masthead.kicker: Hidden Champions of India / a DeepThought series

headline.text: Unisem Agritech: a wealth-creation engine that just went public, on a nine-year-old seed business.

subhead.text: A Karnataka hybrid-seed house that doubled profit in a year, listed on the BSE SME platform in December 2025.

snapshot.label: IPO
snapshot.value: ₹21.45 Cr fresh issue · BSE SME, Dec 2025

blocks.text: Revenue grew from ₹46.91 Cr (FY23) to ₹69.08 Cr (FY25), and PAT nearly doubled year-on-year in FY25 alone, ₹2.15 Cr to ₹4.27 Cr (+98%), with EBITDA climbing from ₹4.03 Cr to ₹7.10 Cr over the same year.

Return on equity is reported at 57-62% (two DRHP-derived figures from different summaries) with ROCE at 38.89% — genuinely strong, though as with Eldorado Agritech's own pre-IPO figures, a small, pre-IPO equity base flatters ROE specifically; the post-listing equity base will be a fairer read going forward.

Note: screener.in shows materially different figures on a different consolidation/restatement basis (FY24 ₹50.31 Cr, FY25 ₹58.38 Cr, FY26 ₹81.03 Cr) — this profile uses the DRHP-sourced figures as primary since they trace to the regulatory filing, but the discrepancy is real and worth resolving before publishing.

It listed on the BSE SME platform in December 2025 (₹21.45 Cr fresh issue, ₹63-65/share price band, 2.28x subscribed) — but the stock opened flat with no listing premium, and proceeds are earmarked for working capital, debt repayment, and expanding seed-processing capacity, R&D and distribution.

R&D runs on 30+ acres of farmland plus lab facilities using genetic markers, QTL mapping and marker-assisted selection, recognized by both the Indian Institute of Horticultural Research and DSIR — the HVT sheet flags this pillar `needs_verify: yes` despite the dual recognition claim.

insights.point: The field is **large, with estimates that genuinely disagree by nearly 2x.**
insights.evidence: Global hybrid seed market: $25.6-30.9B (2025/26) on the conservative count, to $59.7-65.1B (2025) on the bullish count — a wider spread than most segments in this batch. India's domestic seed market: $8.6B (2025) to $20.2B by 2034.
insights.source: Mordor Intelligence; Expert Market Research; IMARC Group

insights.evidence: True F1 hybrids require near-100% annual repurchase since farm-saved seed loses yield potential (heterosis) — a stronger recurring-demand structure than the ~15% national fresh-seed rate that blends in self-pollinated crops.

insights.point: **Export markets closely match where Unisem already has partnerships.**
insights.evidence: Bangladesh, Ghana and Sri Lanka together account for ~74% of India's hybrid seed export shipments — and Unisem's own stated partner markets (Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Botswana, other African markets) sit squarely inside that pattern.

insights.point: Listed peers are **15-20x its scale, but not necessarily healthier.**
insights.evidence: Kaveri Seed (₹1,202 Cr revenue, 18% ROE, 24% EBITDA margin) is the clean at-scale benchmark; Nuziveedu Seeds shows genuinely inconsistent figures across sources (ROE reported as low as -2.85% in one pull), suggesting scale alone doesn't guarantee Unisem's current profitability profile.

reflect.text: A newly-listed, fast-compounding hybrid seed house whose export partnerships already sit in exactly the countries that absorb most of India's hybrid seed exports. The scale gap to Kaveri Seed is real, but the growth rate is running well ahead of it.

p2_market.sourceNote: Market data: Mordor Intelligence, Expert Market Research, IMARC Group, Volza trade data. Peer data: screener.in (Kaveri Seed), Tofler (Nuziveedu Seeds, flagged as inconsistent across sources).

p3_opportunities.lede: One clear place worth watching, named directly in the company's own gap research.

items.title: Beyond 2 verified export buyers
items.body: The HVT sheet's own gap research names this precisely: Unisem's export trade data shows 46 shipments but only 2 verified buyers, across markets that already align with where India's hybrid seed exports concentrate (Bangladesh, Ghana, Sri Lanka). The partnerships exist; the buyer base within them is thin.

guesslabel.text: Possibilities, not prescriptions. Which would work, and how much, only Unisem's own data and people can tell. Each is small, made to learn fast.

items.title: Convert the existing export code into 3-5 new buyers in one market
items.body: Rather than opening new geographies, use IPO proceeds earmarked for distribution to find 3-5 new buyers within the two markets (Bangladesh, Botswana) where relationships already exist, before spending on new-market entry.

takeaway.text: A profit nearly doubled in a year, a fresh public listing, and an export relationship in exactly the right two countries — that's only reaching two actual buyers so far. **The market fit is proven; the buyer base isn't built out yet.**
